content: <thought>From the spectrum, the M+2 peak is about 33 % of the base peak, which matches the characteristic 3:1 intensity ratio of a single chlorine atom (35Cl/37Cl). No ~1:1 M+2 pattern (bromine) or a small ~4 % M+2 (sulfur) is observed. The relatively strong M+1 peak (~16 % of M) is consistent with the natural 1.1 % 13C abundance multiplied by many carbon atoms, indicating the presence of carbon. No other element shows a distinctive isotopic pattern in this data. Therefore, chlorine and carbon can be definitively identified.
